tasks.short: Supervise students in projects and the workshop, visit or call placement companies, record supervision notes and sign-offs, plan placement visits and lab sessions, and answer practical placement questions.

steps.what: Vocational teacher supervises independent or group projects and laboratory work
Vocational teacher plans placement visits and lab sessions by e-mail
Vocational teacher visits or calls companies about field placements
Vocational teacher records supervision notes and skill sign-offs on paper
Vocational teacher answers practical placement questions from students

tasks.design: Supervision notes and skill sign-offs go into the student's e-portfolio ({LMS}) on a phone. Placement companies and students book visit slots in the teacher's booking calendar ({CALENDAR}), and a placement FAQ page answers practical questions on forms, hours and insurance. Supervising students and visiting companies stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sign-offs were paper, visits planned by e-mail and the same questions answered each term.
tasks.enabler_now: E-portfolios, booking calendars and FAQ pages are standard in vocational education.
tasks.still_hard: Placement companies are busy and hard to reach.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing in the workshop that a student is ready for a harder job.

evidence.claim: E-portfolios, booking calendars and FAQ pages are standard tools in vocational education.

assumptions: Boundary: from student projects to questions answered; grading is outside.
Input contract: FAQ kept by the placement office; fallback is e-mail and paper.
Supervising and visiting do not change.
Companies book a slot in about the time an e-mail took; no added time.
research_questions: Do placement questions by e-mail fall?

incremental.description: Vocational teacher keeps the placement FAQ current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few placements; high: many students on placement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Map academic and vocational learning outcomes, align topics and timing with colleagues, write integrated assignments, check them with the team, and publish them.

steps.what: Vocational teacher maps academic and vocational learning outcomes in a spreadsheet
Vocational teacher meets colleagues to integrate academic and vocational curricula
Vocational teacher writes integrated assignments so students obtain a variety of skills

loop.input: The agreed alignment, the academic and vocational learning outcomes and the project theme.
loop.output: Draft assignments that combine both sets of outcomes.
loop.check: Code checks each assignment maps to at least one outcome code from each curriculum; the teacher edits and approves.
loop.stop: Stops when the mapping passes and the teacher approves, or after two failed redrafts the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Combining a maths outcome with a workshop task needs a realistic scenario in prose.

steps.what: Vocational teacher checks the final assignments with the team
Vocational teacher uploads the assignments for students

tasks.design: Learning outcomes of both curricula sit in a curriculum map in the learning environment ({LMS}) that shows which outcomes each assignment covers and where gaps are. A bounded step drafts integrated assignments from the agreed alignment; code checks each covers outcomes from both curricula, and the teacher edits. Once the team has checked them, the assignments are published. Aligning with colleagues stays with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outcomes were mapped in spreadsheets and assignments written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Curriculum maps in learning environments; language models draft assignments.
tasks.still_hard: Academic and workshop teachers plan on different rhythms.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the workshop job that makes a fraction mean something.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits assignment drafts instead of writing from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether students see why the subject matters.

evidence.claim: Curriculum maps in learning environments show outcome coverage; language models can draft assignments from outcomes.
Drafting assignments is not an Annex III use; AI that evaluates learning outcomes is.

assumptions: Boundary: from the curricula to assignments published; grading is outside.
Input contract: outcomes from both curricula in the map; fallback is spreadsheets and writing by hand.
Aligning with colleagues does not change.
No student data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the drafts do teachers keep?

incremental.description: Vocational teacher keeps the curriculum map current.

approvals.approved_version: The assignments as checked with the team in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an existing integrated programme; high: a new programme built from scratch.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search catalogues for books, materials and equipment, select them, make the order list, check it, send it to purchasing, and set up materials in the workshop.

steps.what: Vocational teacher searches catalogues for books, materials and equipment
Vocational teacher selects materials, supplies and equipment for training
Vocational teacher makes the order list and requests quotes
Vocational teacher e-mails the order to purchasing
Vocational teacher assembles and sets up materials in the workshop

tasks.design: Contracted suppliers' catalogues with school prices are searchable in the procurement system ({PROCUREMENT}), so the teacher picks from them instead of collecting quotes. The order list becomes a requisition in the same system, and once the teacher has checked it, it goes to purchasing for approval. Selecting materials and setting up the workshop stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were found in many catalogues and ordered by spreadsheet and e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Procurement systems hold supplier catalogues and requisitions.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist tools are often outside contracted catalogues.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing equipment students will meet in real workplaces.

evidence.claim: Procurement systems hold supplier catalogues with contract prices and turn carts into requisitions.

assumptions: Boundary: from course needs to workshop ready; supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: catalogues loaded by purchasing; fallback is quotes by e-mail.
Selecting and setting up do not change.
Purchasing approves requisitions as it did e-mails.
research_questions: Do orders arrive before the course starts more often?

incremental.description: Vocational teacher asks purchasing to add missing specialist items.

approvals.approved_version: The order as checked by the teacher in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly specialist items outside catalogues; high: standard materials from contracted suppliers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate techniques and procedures in on-the-job training, coach students while they practise, and prepare demonstration materials and instruction cards.

steps.what: Vocational teacher conducts on-the-job training sessions to demonstrate techniques and procedures
Vocational teacher coaches students while they practise
Vocational teacher prepares demonstration materials and instruction cards

tasks.design: Instruction cards and short demonstration videos are shared in a team library ({DOCS}), so teachers reuse rather than remake them. Demonstrating and coaching stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each teacher made own instruction cards.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared libraries and phone video make reuse easy.
tasks.human_edge: Correcting a student's grip before it becomes a habit.

evidence.claim: Shared libraries let teachers reuse instruction cards and short videos.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training session to instruction cards; assessment is outside.
Input contract: library kept by the teaching team; fallback is own cards.
Demonstrating and coaching do not change.

incremental.description: Vocational teacher adds new cards and videos to the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a teacher with own cards; high: a new course.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The vocational teacher keeps supervising, demonstrating, aligning curricula and choosing materials; paper sign-offs, spreadsheets and e-mail orders shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time in the workshop.
